plain: To spread widely, as ideas or rumors

webster.text: To continue or multiply the kind by generation or successive production; applied to animals and plants; as, to propagate a breed of horses or sheep; to propagate any species of fruit tree.

more.text: To spread from person to person; to extend; to give birth to, or originate and spread; as, to propagate a story or report.

example.quote: WILSON prefered the second expedient, he had at one time liked the first best; but as false suggestions may be propagated it should not be made impossible to contradict them.
example.cite: James Madison, Notes of Debates in the Federal Convention of 1787, September 17, 1787
